evidence:
The stated mechanism is real, but the REPRODUCE demonstration cannot complete its required final step against a stated material requirement. At frozen 3abee5a6, src/store/connection.rs:167-175 opens the instance database and invokes initialize; src/store/schema.rs:689-705 applies V36, sets user_version=36 and commits that step, with rollback only on that step's failure. Later steps reach 45 (schema.rs:708-829). At the exact published base 565def86, schema.rs:74 sets LATEST_VERSION=35 and initialize at :428-432 accepts 18..=35 and returns IncompatibleSchema otherwise. Thus stopping the upgraded daemon and replacing only its executable with the base binary indeed cannot reopen that version36-or-later database. This establishes the described mechanism, not the requested ISSUE's materiality.

The applicable migration contract is forward upgrade, retained-data preservation and per-migration failure atomicity. The root design at docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-10-handoff-delivery-redesign/2026-10-10-handoff-delivery-redesign-design.md:24 requires upgrading outstanding obligations while preserving running deadlines, terminal states, provenance and immutable requests/digests; :114 and :126 require genuine populated upgrade/rollback/reopen while keeping released SQL exact. The later v0.9 composition contract clarifies that each historical path executes Main32..35 then new36..45 once, 'preserving per-migration atomicity, FK restore, verification and clock behavior' (resume-main-v090-schema-impact.md:19), and requires an induced rollback followed by reopen and latest verification (:75-81). The concrete published35 test matches that interpretation: tests/store/schema.rs:8190-8207 deliberately fails migration37 after migration36 committed and explicitly expects version36, then :8224-8226 repairs the obstruction and resumes forward initialization. This is not an expectation to restore version35 or to reopen with the old executable.

The surrounding old-reader contract also deliberately fails closed on unknown schema versions: docs/design/herdr-threads/2026-09-27-herdr-threads--store-design.md:17 requires a health error without replacement, and the normative shared-contract-amendment-adopted.md:33 requires preserving incompatible files and rejecting unknown versions. The unchanged preservation test tests/store/schema.rs:2113-2128 expects IncompatibleSchema and leaves the unknown version intact. The exact base itself already uses separately committed forward migration steps (base schema.rs:653-669,674-689), rather than a reverse migration interface. The local upgrade limits are explicit: TRUST-POLICY.md:1559-1568 accepts one-time schema startup work before healthy deadline processing resumes, and :1604-1609 says earlier experimental redesign stamps are not reinterpreted. None of these requires reverse compatibility, an automatic pre-upgrade snapshot, or successful executable-only rollback after a committed version step.

Existing deployment support does not supply the missing promise. docs/install.md:388-396 documents stop/install/ensure and retained state with the newer executable; :35 describes recovery of a failed package-directory swap, not database reversal after ensure. The root design :80 excludes deployment from this implementation tree. The changed warning src/harness/setup.rs:3282-3284 names the hook-command downgrade prerequisite; the base already had the same prerequisite for --event at its :2942-2945. It does not claim that unsetup converts database versions. Therefore the story fails precisely when it treats old-executable reopen after a successful schema upgrade as a required supported recovery path. No loss of retained data, failure of the new binary to resume, or contradiction of the specified failed-step rollback/forward-reopen contract is demonstrated. Internal structural claim; no outside-world premise or runtime execution was needed.
